events.text: The Athenæum was published in London, England starting in 1828.

events.quote: published in London , England from 1828 to 1921

events.text: The Athenæum ceased publication in 1921.

events.quote: published in London , England from 1828 to 1921

events.text: The Athenaeum was initiated by James Silk Buckingham.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Initiated in 1828 by James Silk Buckingham

events.text: It was sold within a few weeks to Frederick Maurice and John Sterling.
events.subject: self
events.quote: it was sold within a few weeks to Frederick Maurice and John Sterling

events.text: Charles Wentworth Dilke became part proprietor and editor.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1829 , Charles Wentworth Dilke became part proprietor and editor

events.text: Dilke resigned the editorship.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1846 , he resigned the editorship

events.text: Thomas Kibble Hervey succeeded Dilke as editor.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Thomas Kibble Hervey succeeded Dilke as editor and served from 1846

events.text: Hervey resigned due to ill health.
events.subject: self
events.quote: his resignation due to ill health in 1853

events.text: William Hepworth Dixon succeeded Hervey as editor.

events.quote: William Hepworth Dixon succeeded Hervey in 1853

events.text: Dixon remained editor until 1869.

events.quote: remained editor until 1869

events.text: Gerald Massey contributed many literary reviews during the period 1858 to 1868.

events.text: Theodore Watts-Dunton contributed regularly as the principal critic of poetry from 1879.

events.text: Frederic George Stephens was art editor from 1860.

events.text: The Athenaeum was incorporated into the Nation, becoming The Nation and Athenaeum.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1921 , with decreasing circulation , the Athenaeum was incorporated into its younger competitor : the Nation , becoming The Nation and Athenaeum .

events.text: The successor publication merged with the New Statesman to form the New Statesman and Nation.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1931 , this successor publication merged with the New Statesman , to form the New Statesman and Nation

events.text: The name Athenaeum was eliminated after 97 years.
